name: base-kernel
description: Which kernel this machine boots. Exactly one — a host takes `stable` or `latest`, never both. Every host here boots an encrypted ZFS root, so the kernel and the OpenZFS module must come from the same package set; each member below pairs them itself.

choiceWarning.latest: 7.2 comes from nixpkgs-master, which is not on Hydra: this host will compile its own kernel and ZFS module, and again on every master pin bump. Budget hours for the next rebuild.

choiceDetails.stable: The kernel the pinned nixpkgs calls default, with the OpenZFS from that same nixpkgs. nixpkgs marks an incompatible kernel/ZFS pair broken at evaluation, so this arrangement cannot produce a machine that boots but cannot import its pool. Both halves are prebuilt on Hydra.
choiceDetails.latest: Kernel 7.2 with OpenZFS 2.4.4, both from nixpkgs-master — the only place that pair exists, since the pinned nixpkgs ships 2.4.3 whose ceiling is kernel 7.0. master is pre-Hydra, so this host compiles BOTH the kernel and the ZFS module itself, and again whenever the master pin moves. master is a moving branch: a flake.lock update can land a pair nobody has run yet. Rollback is the previous generation in GRUB, which carries its own matching pair.
